ety.text: * From гор(а́) (gor(á)) + -ец (-ec). * From an accentological point of view from adjective го́р(ский) (gór(skij)) + -ец (-ec), which allows us to explain the root stress. Whereas a direct connection of the stem of the word гора́ (gorá) and the suffix -ец (-ec) should have given *горе́ц (*goréc), that is, the stress го́рец (górec) would have to be considered an exception.
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gorьcь, substantivisation of a variant of *gorьkъ with progressive palatalisation.

s.g: short past adverbial participle of заа́грить (zaágritʹ)
beater (a person who drives game towards shooters in a hunting party, often working in a group)

и овцы целы, и волки сыты.w: и овцы целы, и волки сыты

s.g: Used when a win-win mutual agreement is found.

ety.text: Literally, “the sheep [are] safe, and the wolves [are] full”. Compare Polish wilk syty i owca cała.

s.g: to slog through, to crank through, to work through (to process, do or implement in large quantities)
Louisiana (a state in the Deep South and South Central regions of the United States)
cheaply, at a very low price, for nothing

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic обличье (obličĭje), from Proto-Slavic *obličьje, from *oblikъ + *-ьje, from *ob- + *likъ. Cognate with Belarusian аблі́чча (ablíčča), Ukrainian обли́ччя (oblýččja). By surface analysis, о́блик (óblik) + -ье (-ʹje).

s.g: to revive, to bring back (of something that has been lost or forgotten)
to imbue physical or emotional energy (ex. into a person, a street)
to improve the appearance (ex. of a building)

x: Для бы́строго образова́ния ко́рочки при обжа́ривании о́вощи, осо́бенно карто́фель, необходи́мо хорошо́ отсуши́ть на салфе́тке.

s.g: to stop, to cease, to quit
OK, so-so (in answer to the question, "как дела?" ("How are you?"), the response "потихоньку"—"OK" or "I'm getting along okay"—implies that things could be better and could be worse)

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic пришьствиѥ (prišĭstvije), пришествиѥ (prišestvije). By surface analysis, прише́д (prišéd) + -ствие (-stvije).

x: Скажи́, что я её люблю́ Без неё вся жизнь равна́ нулю́

Что легче? сказать ли расслабленному: «прощаются тебе грехи»? или сказать: «встань, возьми свою постель и ходи»? Što lexče? skazatʹ li rasslablennomu: «proščajutsja tebe grexi»? ili skazatʹ: «vstanʹ, vozʹmi svoju postelʹ i xodi»?

ety.text: Perfective form of archaic Russian каза́ть (kazátʹ), from Proto-Slavic *kazati.

s.g: to chant; to scan; to cry out

x: – Вспо́мнил! Вспо́мнил! В Пу́шкино откры́лась чебуре́чная «Я́лта»! Всё поня́тно! Пое́хал туда́, напи́лся и тепе́рь отту́да телеграфи́рует!

s.g: a male surname, Shulgin, originating as a patronymic, feminine equivalent Шульги́на (Šulʹgína)

ety.text: Borrowed from German Edelweiß, from edel + Weiß.
